payload.executive_summary: Candidate B02A selects architecture option O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in) to minimize wall-clock time by executing independent implementation lanes in parallel while preserving CouncilOS governance: deterministic orchestration, strict role separation, RFC6901 evidence pointers, RFC6902 JSON Patch repairs, diff-only patchsets, and a dedicated deterministic integration/validation stage before Judge→Freeze. This candidate emphasizes integration-risk mitigation (notably merge conflicts K12 and integration regressions) via deterministic merge ordering, integration-level full validators, and integration-focused review/patch loops under medium HITL strictness concentrated on integration and policy exceptions.

architecture_choice.rationale: O2 best matches the branch goal of speed via parallelizable work while remaining compatible with non-negotiable governance constraints: orchestrator-owned DAG scheduling/budgets (CNS1), immutable audit spine and checkpointing (R8), lane-scoped JSON-only artifact outputs (R9), and a deterministic fan-in integration stage that absorbs the main tradeoff (higher integration complexity) with explicit conflict handling (K12), full-repo validation gates (R21), and integration review before Judge→Freeze. The hybrid milestone strategy is implemented by treating each lane’s completion as an intermediate milestone with its own scoped gates, followed by a single deterministic Integration milestone as the final fan-in gate that must pass system-level validators prior to Freeze.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: Intake validates plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json and initializes run_manifest/event_log/workspace_index → Work planner produces work_plan.json with DAG partitioning into lanes → Per-lane sub-state-machines run Generate→(PatchApply)→Validate→Review→Patch loops producing lane-scoped patchsets + lane validation outputs + lane findings + stage_handoffs → Integration Merge Engine deterministically applies completed lane patchsets to a shared integrated repo state (independent of wall-clock completion) and emits conflict/integration reports → Integration Validator runs full-repo gates and emits integrated test_results/quality reports → Integration Review/Patch iterates under bounded caps → Judge evaluates integrated state + all findings/trace, emits trace_report and freeze recommendation → Freeze Assembler validates closure gates and assembles the Implementation Freeze Bundle (including stage_handoffs/ and context_packs/), then emits decision_record and release_bundle.
key_design_decisions: Use deterministic lane partitioning and lane-scoped context packs to reduce context pressure while enabling parallelism; lane outputs remain fully auditable and indexed.
Require deterministic fan-in merge ordering rules that do not depend on lane completion time; integration is the single source of integrated truth for Judge→Freeze.
Run two-tier validation: lane-scoped validators for fast feedback plus integration-level full validators as the controlling freeze gate.
Concentrate HITL on policy exceptions, protected-path touches, security-critical findings, and unresolved integration conflicts; keep lane loops primarily automated with bounded retries.
Treat workspace as namespaced partitions (per-lane + integration) with a unified workspace_index.json and mandatory stage_handoffs at every checkpoint boundary.

milestones.name: Intake + DAG Work Planning (Fan-out Ready)

deliverables.text: Validated inputs: plan_package_final.json accepted as sole canonical planning input; repo_context.json and workspace_context.json schema-valid and present before any writing stages.
Initialized audit spine artifacts: immutable implementation_run_manifest.json and append-only implementation_event_log.jsonl, with an Intake→Parallel stage_handoff emitted.
work_plan.json compiled with dependency DAG and lane partitioning hints suitable for deterministic parallel execution and later deterministic merge ordering.

exit_criteria: AT1, AT2, AT3 pass (input authority, repo_context gate, workspace_context gate).
AT4 and AT5 preconditions established: stage sequence defined and stage_handoff requirement enforceable at transitions.
No intake validator flags requiring reroute upstream for plan ambiguity/completeness (risk K20).

milestones.name: Parallel Lanes Execute (Generate→Validate→Review→Patch per Lane)

deliverables.text: For each lane: diff-only patchset artifacts produced with explicit base_commit and deterministic apply ordering metadata; lane artifacts indexed in workspace_index.json with provenance.
For each lane: lane-scoped validation outputs (test_results.json, quality_reports.json) produced via declared repo_context entrypoints; deterministic retry policy applied and recorded.
For each lane: findings-only review_findings.json with RFC6901 evidence pointers; no reviewer emits patches or writing artifacts.
Per-lane stage_handoffs emitted at every lane checkpoint boundary, capturing resumable state and evidence pointers into lane artifacts.

exit_criteria: AT9 (JSON-only/schema-valid outputs) holds for all lane artifacts.
AT13 and AT14 constraints enforced: code changes are diff-only patchsets; forbidden/protected paths and op caps enforced and violations recorded.
AT19 enforcement demonstrated: tool invocations outside lane permissions blocked and logged.
AT20 secrets guardrails pass at each lane checkpoint (no secrets persisted).

milestones.name: Lane Completion Gates + Readiness for Fan-in

deliverables.text: Lane completion signals emitted with immutable references to each lane’s accepted patchsets, validation outputs, and findings, ready for deterministic integration collection.
Conflict risk pre-check outputs (overlap/protected-path touch reports) produced as structured artifacts to inform integration ordering and early escalation when needed.

exit_criteria: All lanes pass their scoped gates per acceptance strategy (lane-level validators + findings triage completed).
Any lane failures exceeding deterministic retry budgets are escalated per policy path (patch → reroute → HITL → ChangeRequest) with event_log entries (R23).

milestones.name: Deterministic Integration (Fan-in Merge/Validate/Review/Patch)

deliverables.text: Integration Merge Engine applies completed lane patchsets in deterministic order to base repo state, emitting merged repo_snapshot.json plus structured conflict/integration report(s) when applicable.

Integration Validator emits integrated test_results.json and quality_reports.json for full-repo gates; regressions and cross-lane interaction issues captured as structured failures with evidence pointers.
Integration Review produces findings-only integration review_findings.json focusing on cross-lane coupling, protected-path touches, and system-level quality.

Integration Patch loop (bounded) produces integration-level repair artifacts (replacement patchsets and/or RFC6902 patches for JSON artifacts) until all integration gates pass or escalation triggers fire.

exit_criteria: Integration conflicts (K12) either resolved within deterministic thresholds/op caps or escalated with packaged conflict summary per policy.
All required system-level closure gates are passing in the integrated state (R21), subject to deterministic retry/quarantine policy (R23).
Stage_handoff artifacts emitted for each integration checkpoint boundary and indexed (R5/R18).

milestones.name: Judge: Trace Completeness + Governance Closure (Integrated State)

deliverables.text: trace_report.json produced across lanes + integration, validating RFC6901 evidence pointers resolve to versioned JSON artifacts and that AT# coverage mapping is present where required.
Decision inputs assembled: integrated validation results, all lane + integration findings, risk closure assessment against K# register, and any required ChangeRequest/waiver artifacts (if triggered).

exit_criteria: No decision clause lacks evidence pointers (K18 mitigation), and any waiver/exception is routed to required HITL triggers.
Trace completeness gate passes: evidence-pointer linting and pointer resolution succeed, and AT# mapping policy satisfied (R10/R11/R25).

milestones.name: Freeze: Assemble Implementation Freeze Bundle (Single Integrated Freeze)

deliverables.text: Implementation Freeze Bundle assembled with all minimum artifacts/directories: implementation_run_manifest.json, implementation_event_log.jsonl, work_plan.json, patchsets/, repo_snapshot.json, test_results.json, quality_reports.json, trace_report.json, review_findings.json, release_bundle.json, decision_record.json, workspace_index.json, context_packs/, stage_handoffs/.
Final integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity validation pass report recorded; secrets scan passes prior to persistence of freeze outputs.

exit_criteria: AT7 and AT21 pass: freeze bundle is complete and freeze is permitted only when all required gates pass.
AT8 pass conditions maintained: run manifest immutable; event log append-only; artifacts versioned; checkpoints recorded at stage boundaries.

decision_log.question: Which architecture option best fits the branch’s speed-first posture while preserving deterministic governance and a single integrated freeze outcome?
decision_log.choice: Select O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in with a deterministic integration sub-flow).
decision_log.rationale: The branch explicitly prioritizes wall-clock speed via divisible parallel work while accepting higher integration complexity. O2 directly supports parallel lanes with lane-scoped gates and a dedicated deterministic integration stage to manage merge conflicts (K12) and integration regressions before Judge→Freeze, aligning with the hybrid milestone strategy and two-level acceptance strategy.
what_would_change_this_decision: If target repos are highly coupled and integration conflicts are frequent enough that O2’s fan-in dominates wall-clock time or escalations (K12).
If operational budgets or model portfolio constraints make parallel lanes prohibitively expensive, pushing toward O1/O3.
If deterministic merge ordering and lane partitioning cannot be made independent of wall-clock completion timing (reproducibility concern).

evidence_pointers.note: Architecture option O2 definition (parallel lanes + deterministic integration).
Branch rationale emphasizes speed via parallelism and managing integration risk.

decision_log.question: How is determinism preserved when parallel lanes complete at different times?
decision_log.choice: Define merge/fan-in determinism as an explicit policy: integration applies completed lane patchsets in a deterministic order independent of completion time, using each patchset’s declared base_commit and an orchestrator-owned ordering rule.
decision_log.rationale: O2’s main reproducibility hazard is nondeterministic merge ordering driven by wall-clock completion timing. A deterministic integration ordering plus strict base_commit requirements directly mitigates this risk and aligns with K12 mitigation requirements.
alternatives_considered: Apply lanes in completion order (rejected: nondeterministic).
Attempt automatic conflict resolution without strict thresholds (rejected: safety/governance risk).
Disallow parallelism entirely (rejected: contradicts branch goal).
what_would_change_this_decision: If repo ecosystems require a different deterministic merge primitive than patchset application (e.g., strictly rebases), while still meeting R13/R14 constraints.
If upstream defines a canonical merge ordering or integration strategy that must be followed.

evidence_pointers.note: K12 integration/merge conflict risk and deterministic merge ordering mitigation.
R13 diff-only patchsets with deterministic apply order requirement.

decision_log.question: What is the validation strategy to balance speed and integration safety under parallelism?
decision_log.choice: Use two-tier validation: lane-scoped validators for fast feedback and integration-level full-repo validators as the controlling freeze gates.
decision_log.rationale: Lane-level validation reduces feedback latency and allows parallel progress, but cannot guarantee cross-lane safety. Integration-level full validators (build/test/lint/typecheck/security/secrets, as applicable) ensure the integrated state meets closure gates required for freeze.
alternatives_considered: Lane-only validation (rejected: risks missing cross-lane regressions).
Full-repo validation in every lane (rejected: likely too slow/costly; defeats parallelism benefits).
No integration review stage (rejected: weak governance for fan-in risk).
what_would_change_this_decision: If repo_context mandates full-repo validation for any change due to safety/compliance constraints.
If lane partitioning cannot reliably scope validators (ecosystem limitation).

evidence_pointers.note: R21 closure gates required before freeze.
Validate stage policy: declared entrypoints, deterministic retries, security/secrets scanning.

decision_log.question: How are role separation and findings-only reviewer constraints enforced across parallel lanes and integration?
decision_log.choice: Enforce role separation via orchestrator routing constraints per lane and per integration stage, with reviewers limited to findings-only artifacts and judges limited to decisions-only artifacts; record model/vendor provenance in run manifest for separation checks.
decision_log.rationale: Parallelism increases the number of role invocations and therefore the chance of accidental role mixing. Enforcing strict output-type allowlists and routing separation across lanes/integration preserves CNS12/R22 and reduces governance risk (K10).
alternatives_considered: Allow the same model/vendor to write and review within a lane (rejected: independence failure).
Allow reviewers to propose patches directly (rejected: violates findings-only constraint).
what_would_change_this_decision: If the available model portfolio cannot satisfy multi-vendor separation in some environments (would require explicit policy exception/HITL and alternative controls).

evidence_pointers.note: R22 role separation and multi-vendor requirement.
K10 role separation failure risk and mitigation.

decision_log.question: What checkpoint/resume boundary artifacts are mandatory under parallelism?
decision_log.choice: Require stage_handoff artifacts at every stage transition for each lane and for the integration/global transitions, with pointers into work_plan, patchsets, and validation outputs; enforce via validators and workspace indexing.
decision_log.rationale: O2 introduces multiple concurrent state machines (lanes) plus integration. Deterministic resume requires explicit, machine-verifiable state capture at each boundary (R5/R6) and complete workspace indexing (R18) across partitions.
alternatives_considered: Only global stage handoffs (rejected: insufficient for per-lane resume).
Allow implicit resume via event log replay without explicit handoffs (rejected: violates R5/R6 intent).
what_would_change_this_decision: If orchestrator design explicitly replaces stage_handoff with a different canonical resume artifact (would require upstream schema changes).

evidence_pointers.note: R5 stage_handoff required at every checkpoint boundary.
R6 stage_handoff content requirements (cold-start resume fields + evidence pointers).
R18 workspace_index completeness and context pack bounds enforcement.

synthesis_warnings.summary: O2 integration determinism and conflict-resolution thresholds depend on unspecified merge strategy and patchset diff format/normalization; these are currently blocking to fully specify deterministic fan-in behavior.

evidence.note: Q7: patchset diff format + normalization rules needed for deterministic application.
Q9: conflict resolution and merge strategy for overlapping patchsets.

synthesis_warnings.summary: Parallel-lane validation scoping and required default validators are blocked by unspecified target repo ecosystems and mandatory-vs-optional validation policy; this affects lane partitioning, tool permissions, and gate completeness for O2.

evidence.note: Q1: target repository ecosystems and mandatory validations.
Q11: network/package-manager handling under policies (reproducibility constraints).

synthesis_warnings.summary: Tool permission matrix and protected/forbidden path enforcement require a concrete repo_context.json schema definition for path patterns and high-risk operations; without it, protected-path HITL triggers and patch_apply enforcement cannot be fully validated.

evidence.note: Q14: required schema for repo_context.json protected/forbidden paths and enforcement details.
Q4: forbidden/protected paths and what constitutes high-risk operations requiring HITL.
